# ProgressBar

`ProgressBar` — a determinate (or indeterminate) bar for a task whose proportion done is known. `value` is a percent (0 to 100); the drawn width and the announced `aria-valuenow` clamp together, so an out-of-range value never draws a full bar while reporting a number past its own `aria-valuemax` (#325) — a state no assistive technology can make sense of.

Also asked as: percent complete, determinate loading.

**Import:** `import { ProgressBar } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/loading/ProgressBar/ProgressBar.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/loading/ProgressBar/ProgressBar.stories.jsx` — Overview, Appearances, Default, Success, Inverse, WithACaption, Indeterminate, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/loading/ProgressBar/ProgressBar.mdx`

**Motion:** change `linear` · success `appearance.fast`, sound `sound.done.step`. Read the tokens through `--ds-motion-*`; see Foundations · Motion.

## Usage

Use `ProgressBar` for progress through a task: an upload, a course, a
multi-step form. When the task's length is unknown, set `isIndeterminate`. For
a short wait with no task to track, use a `Spinner`.

### Appearance guidance

| Appearance | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Default | Most bars: a brand fill on a neutral track. |
| Success | Marks completion. Show a finished task at 100 in success. |
| Inverse | On a bold or colored background. |

## Motion

ProgressBar reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Load content | `--ds-motion-linear` | Fills with the work, never ahead of it. |  |
| success | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | The bar reaches its end and its fill changes to done. | `sound.done.step` on land: a module or lesson is done |

## Best practices

### Indeterminate when the length is unknown. {#indeterminate-when-the-length-is-unknown}

A bar that fills implies a known total; use the moving bar when the work has
no measurable end. `isIndeterminate` drops `value` and the value attributes.

### Use inverse on bold surfaces. {#use-inverse-on-bold-surfaces}

The default track disappears on a bold ground; inverse keeps the bar readable.

Do: Inverse appearance on a bold surface.
Don't: Default appearance on a bold surface.

### One bar per task. {#one-bar-per-task}

Stacked bars for one task read as separate jobs; show a single bar for the whole.

Do: A single bar.
Don't: Three bars for one task.

### Put the number in text beside the bar. {#put-the-number-in-text-beside-the-bar}

The bar is 8 tall and carries no text of its own.

Do: A caption beside the bar says what the fill means.
Don't: A bare bar leaves the reader to guess the number.

### Show a finished task as success. {#show-a-finished-task-as-success}

Do: At 100, the success appearance marks the task done.
Don't: A finished task left as a brand bar.

## Accessibility

- **The bar is a real progressbar.** `role="progressbar"` with
  `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` when determinate, and
  an `aria-label` that defaults to "Progress".
- **Reduced motion is handled.** The indeterminate sweep stops under
  `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- **Color is not the message.** `appearance` colors the bar and says nothing
  to a screen reader; the `ariaLabel` and a caption carry the meaning.

## Related

- For an indeterminate wait with no track at all, use `Spinner`.
- For the outcome when it finishes, use `Flag` or `SectionMessage`.
- For position in a hierarchy rather than progress through a task, use `Breadcrumb`.

Same group: `GenerativeBorder` · `Skeleton` · `Spinner`

## Parts

1. **Track.** The full-width bar the fill runs along, a pill 8 tall.
2. **Fill.** The done part, a percent of the track. Indeterminate, it is a moving segment.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | Determinate: the fill width is `value`, clamped to 0 to 100 together with `aria-valuenow`. |
| Indeterminate | A segment slides along the track. No value is announced. Under reduced motion the segment holds still. |
| Hovered | None. It is not a control. |
| Pressed | None. |
| Focused | None. It is not in the tab order. |
| Disabled | None. A bar has no disabled state. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Track | `--ds-background-neutral`, `--progress-bar-height` tall, `--radius-full`. |
| Fill | `--ds-background-brand-bold` through `--plus-progressbar-fill-color`; `--ds-background-success-bold` for `success`. |
| Inverse | Track `--ds-background-inverse-subtle`, fill `--ds-background-inverse-subtle-pressed`. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the bar for what it measures: "68% of goals met". | Leave the default "Progress" label. |
| Use the same words in the caption and in `ariaLabel`: "68% of goals met". | Say one thing on screen and another to a screen reader. |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `value` | number | `0` | A percent, 0 to 100 |
| `appearance` | enum | `'default'` | success marks completion; inverse reads on a bold background |
| `isIndeterminate` | bool | `false` | The duration is unknown |
| `ariaLabel` | string | `'Progress'` | Names what the bar measures. "Progress" says nothing when a page has two bars. |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `id` | string | — | — |
